title: What a Cracked Fitting From Frozen Irrigation Lines Costs You
meta_title: What a Cracked Fitting From Frozen Lines Costs You
meta_description: A single fitting cracked by frozen water can turn a healthy sprinkler system into a full spring repair project. Here's why the damage tends to add up fast.
lede: A cracked fitting sounds like a small problem. What it actually creates once the system runs again in spring usually isn't.
excerpt: Why a single cracked fitting from a hard freeze becomes a bigger repair than it looks.

sections.heading: It's Rarely Just One Fitting
paragraphs: If a hard freeze hit water still sitting in the system, it likely affected more than one location, since the same conditions existed throughout the whole network of pipes at once. A cracked fitting found in one zone is often a sign to check the rest of the system rather than assume it's an isolated issue.

sections.heading: The Damage Is Underground
paragraphs: Fittings and pipe joints are buried, which means a crack doesn't just need a part replaced, it needs the ground opened up to reach it. That's a different kind of repair than something visible above ground, and it's part of why freeze damage tends to be more involved than the size of the actual crack suggests.

sections.heading: It Shows Up at the Worst Possible Time
paragraphs: This kind of damage is discovered in spring, right when the system needs to be running for the season and right when a new lawn or landscaping might depend on it working. A repair that could have been entirely avoided with a fall blowout instead becomes a spring priority.

sections.heading: Why Prevention Is the Cheaper Path
paragraphs: A fall blowout removes the water before a freeze has anything to damage. Once a fitting has already cracked, the only path forward is locating and repairing it, which takes more time and effort than winterizing would have taken in the first place.

faqs.q: If I find one cracked fitting, could there be more damage elsewhere?
faqs.a: It's possible. The same freeze conditions affected the whole system, so one cracked fitting is a reason to check other zones as well.

faqs.q: Why is this kind of repair more involved than it sounds?
faqs.a: Fittings are buried, so reaching one to repair it means opening up the ground around it, not just swapping a visible part.

faqs.q: Is there a way to know I have freeze damage before spring?
faqs.a: Not always. Most freeze damage isn't discovered until the system is run again in spring, which is why prevention through a fall blowout matters.
